specification.problem: Approximate the mean value of a black-box function with quantum algorithms (one novel and asymptotically optimal, one a variation on Aharonov's earlier algorithm), and approximate the median of a set of points over an arbitrary distance function.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level problem statement plus a small finite-instance mean-estimation setting for equations; the algorithmic details of the paper are not given in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: black-box function whose mean is to be approximated

equations.label: Mean value
equations.description: Mean of the black-box function over N points; the standard definition of the target quantity.
equations.justification: The abstract only says 'mean value of a black-box function'; the explicit formula is the standard definition, with domain assumed.
assumptions: Uniform distribution over a finite domain of size N

equations.label: Accuracy goal
equations.description: Target of the approximation: estimate within additive error epsilon.
equations.justification: The abstract does not state the error criterion; additive error is an assumed standard choice.

registers.name: x
registers.role: index register holding a uniform superposition over the domain

specification.initial_state: |0>^{\otimes n}|0> on registers x and a (assumed)

steps.description: Apply Hadamards to x to prepare the uniform superposition over the domain.
Query the oracle for f and rotate ancilla a so that the |1> amplitude squared on branch x is f(x). The probability of measuring a=1 is then mu (assumed encoding).
Apply amplitude estimation (assumed generic subroutine, with about 1/epsilon repetitions of the state-preparation unitary) to estimate mu within epsilon.

specification.measurement: In the placeholder amplitude-estimation sketch, measure the phase/counting register of amplitude estimation in the computational basis (the ancilla a is only used as the marked qubit inside the estimation). The paper's actual measurement scheme is not given in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Convert the measured phase integer y over M outcomes to an amplitude estimate via sin^2(pi y/M), and output it as the estimate of mu; repeat and take the median if higher success probability is needed (assumed standard practice).
assumptions: Finite domain, uniform distribution, f in [0,1]
